public_rationale: On the reading that depreciation consumes current operating growth, all four companies contradict the claim. Their operating income increased after depreciation was charged. Alphabet and Meta also show depreciation increases well below their operating-income increases. A weaker claim that depreciation reduces earnings would be consistent with the records, so the interpretation matters.
limitations: Operating income is the evaluator's chosen growth measure.
The verdict applies to full consumption of growth, not merely an earnings headwind.
The contract covers four separate companies; their scopes and Microsoft's fiscal-quarter designation must be matched component by component.
This does not establish whether the capital investments will earn adequate future returns.

our_interpretation: Use January–March 2026, the latest reported quarter before the post, compared with January–March 2025. For Microsoft this is fiscal Q3.
Read growth as consolidated operating-income growth and 'whatever growth ... is being eaten' as rising depreciation consuming the operating improvement, rather than merely reducing it.
Operating income already includes depreciation. Do not deduct depreciation from reported operating income a second time.
Evaluate each named company separately. The single metric_scope object describes this collection of company-specific tests, not a combined financial statement.
The accounting basis is company_reported because the passage invokes the companies' reported quarterly figures.
